title: Light Martini water accelerates sampling in coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations
abstract: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of slow biomolecular processes, such as exploration of the conformational ensembles of intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs), are computationally demanding. Although coarse-grained (CG) models can substantially speed up the simulations compared to all-atom MD, the sampling challenge can still be significant for large systems and long time scales. Here, we present light Martini water, a low-viscosity water model that accelerates sampling in MD simulations with the Martini CG force field. We systematically reduced the mass of the Martini water beads and verified stable, accurate integration of the equations of motion with 20 fs time steps, as typically used in Martini simulations. Light Martini water has a reduced mass of 20 amu (compared to 72 amu in the standard water model), yielding up to a 2.68-fold increase in the sampling rate of IDP chain reconfiguration in water and a 16% increase in the lateral diffusion of lipids in a palmitoyloleoylphosphatidylcholine bilayer. Equilibrium properties remained unaffected by the mass scaling, and the speedup was achieved without compromising simulation accuracy. The water model is trivial to implement, has no computational overhead, and should be universally applicable to Martini simulations.
relevance_reason: Develops and validates a low-viscosity Martini water model for coarse-grained molecular dynamics, satisfying (a) CG atomistically mapped beads, (b) MD/force-field methodology, and (c) a simulation-method advance.

title: Q-Chem/CP2K software interface for projection-based, pseudoperiodic wavefunction-in-DFT embedding
abstract: We report an implementation of projection-based quantum embedding that combines periodic density functional theory in the CP2K code with correlated wavefunction calculations in the Q-Chem program. Using this interface, correlated wavefunction methods can be applied to a subset of molecular orbitals, selected in an automated manner based on a user-defined list of nuclei, with an embedding potential that provides electronic coupling to the remaining orbitals that comprise the environment. Our implementation uses exact projection, without the need for any level-shift operator, and is “pseudoperiodic” in the sense that periodic boundary effects are implicit in the orbitals used in the (non-periodic) wavefunction calculation. Convergence tests demonstrate that computed properties are faithful to the corresponding periodic quantities, provided that the high-level subsystem is spatially localized and small, relative to the periodic simulation cell. Spectroscopic examples for aqueous chromophores demonstrate converged results using a very limited subset of water molecules in the simulation cell, decoupling the choice of excited-state method and basis set from the functional that is used to propagate ground-state ab initio molecular dynamics. Solvatochromic shifts for aqueous uracil are converged using equation-of-motion coupled-cluster theory, without the need for solvent molecules in the wavefunction calculation, and the embedded calculation captures solvent effects that are absent in gas-phase “microhydration” studies. Additional applications include adsorption of CO on a slab model of Si(100) and bond dissociation in a one-dimensional periodic polymer. In both of the latter cases, the system/environment partition crosses a covalent bond; these applications demonstrate that pseudoperiodic embedding can be applied to realistic systems in materials science.
relevance_reason: Implements projection-based wavefunction-in-DFT embedding coupling periodic DFT with correlated wavefunction calculations and ab initio MD, satisfying (a) explicit atomistic/periodic systems, (b) DFT/embedding methodology, and (c) method development.

title: Assessment of particle-density transformation functions for the optimal determination of the configurational entropy of mixing in molecular liquids
abstract: We critically investigate implementation details of our recently developed approach for the calculation of the configurational entropy of mixing for multicomponent molecular liquids based on atomistic molecular dynamics simulations. In particular, we study the influence of the choice of the function that serves as a transformation from atomic coordinates to a smooth particle density on the numerical results for the entropy of mixing. We find that several common functions perform very well, yielding virtually the same numerical entropy results. A certain care is required for the choice of the central parameter of these functions, which controls the specific width of the spatial broadening for each particle. Our findings confirm the broad applicability of our computational approach for the configurational entropy of mixing for molecular liquids and provide a solid basis for choosing the correct numerical broadening parameters.
relevance_reason: Assesses particle-density transformation functions for configurational entropy of mixing using atomistic molecular dynamics, satisfying (a) explicit atoms, (b) MD/free-energy methodology, and (c) method/application advance.

title: Structural transition in one-dimensional water unveils the origin of multifurcated hydrogen bond weakening
abstract: Water confined to low dimensions exhibits even more anomalous behavior than bulk water. Since these anomalies are primarily dictated by hydrogen bonds (hbs), we investigate hb behavior in quasi-one-dimensional water chains using density functional theory. We show that a water chain with two molecules per unit cell transforms from a single-file (low-linear-density) to a double-file (high-linear-density) structure under uniaxial compression. Furthermore, we show that repulsive interactions emerge when hbs become multifurcated. These additional repulsive forces weaken the hbs and play a crucial role in driving the structural transition. We demonstrate that the many-body interactions associated with hb cooperativity, as well as the repulsive forces from multifurcated hbs, are captured by classical dipole–dipole interactions. This indicates that both hb cooperativity and the weakening of multifurcated hbs are classical electrostatic phenomena, even though quantum effects dictate the strength of the effective dipoles involved. Finally, we discuss how these results provide insights for understanding the flow mechanism of water along pores of sub-nanometer diameter and aid in developing a simple, universal water model.
relevance_reason: Uses DFT to study structural transitions and hydrogen-bond weakening in one-dimensional water chains, satisfying (a) explicit atoms, (b) DFT methodology, and (c) application to an atomistic system.

title: Singlet and triplet excitations in C 5 F 10 O induced by electrons and photons: Spectroscopy and dynamics
abstract: C5F10O [heptafluoroisopropyl(trifluoromethyl)ketone] has emerged as a promising alternative to sulfur hexafluoride for the use in gas-insulated switchgears. Despite its technological relevance, its interactions with low-energy electrons remain largely unexplored. Electron impact can populate both singlet and triplet electronically excited states, potentially initiating dissociation pathways that yield toxic or technologically undesirable products. Here, we combine vacuum-ultraviolet (VUV) absorption spectroscopy, electron energy loss spectroscopy (EELS), and theoretical modeling to characterize the electronically excited states of C5F10O and the dynamics initiated by these excitations. We report the first VUV absorption spectrum of C5F10O and directly compare it to EELS recorded at multiple scattering angles and residual energies. The spectra are compared with high-level ab initio calculations. To obtain the inelastic electron scattering cross sections, we use our implementation of the Born approximation coupled with the algebraic diagrammatic construction of the second order method. An ad hoc extension of this approach is introduced to account for the exchange-mediated spin-forbidden transitions in the spectra of backscattered electrons. Finally, nonadiabatic molecular dynamics coupled with time-dependent density functional theory is used to identify reaction channels initiated in different singlet and triplet excited states. Overall, we provide a state-resolved framework to study electronic excitation and subsequent reactivity, with implications for plasma modeling and the design of next-generation high-voltage insulation media.
relevance_reason: Combines spectroscopy with high-level ab initio calculations and nonadiabatic molecular dynamics coupled to TDDFT to study excited-state reaction channels, satisfying (a) explicit atoms, (b) MD/ab initio methodology, and (c) application.
